transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-30 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58m
Attendees: Maya, Liam (Redwood); Sofia, Rajat, Emily, Tom (OpalView)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on this account. We've got Liam here, our SE, who will walk through the technical bits. Sofia, thanks for organizing.
[00:12] Sofia Martinez: Yeah thanks, happy to be here. We've been looking at improving search relevance across product and help docs, so curious to see the embeddings + reranker pattern you mentioned.
[00:20] Liam O'Connor: Cool, thanks. Quick agenda: show the Console playground, then the hosted embeddings API, then the reranker endpoint pattern — how you do candidate retrieval + rerank — and finally run a small live example with a sample dataset. We have some latency and cost numbers to discuss too.
[00:34] Emily Zhou: Sounds good. Our main constraints are sub-200ms query latency for UI, and cost under X per month — we have a hard cap the finance team gave us, so we need to understand unit economics.
[00:47] Rajat Kapoor: Also curious about throughput for batch reindexing and whether you support async scoring. We run nightly reindex jobs and sometimes need to re-embed 2M docs.
[00:58] Liam O'Connor: Yep, good notes. For hosted mode we do both synchronous and async jobs — batching, and a bulk embeddings endpoint. Nightly reindexing often uses dedicated batch windows; we can discuss Dedicated capacity later if needed.
[01:12] Maya Chen: Quick ask: could you share who owns the pilot internally? Just helps with access and expectations.
[01:19] Sofia Martinez: I'll be the project owner; Emily will own product metrics; Rajat will be our integration lead.
[01:25] Liam O'Connor: Great. I'll jump into the Console. (screen share)
[01:32] (screen share noises, brief pause)
[01:40] Liam O'Connor: Here is the Console playground. On the left you can call the embeddings endpoint with a sample payload, see token usage and cost estimate. Note the per-route telemetry shows median latency and p50/p95 — it's handy for UI SLAs.
[01:56] Rajat Kapoor: That p95 graph — is that per-token or per-request?
[02:02] Liam O'Connor: Per-request. It includes network and inference time. We also expose per-token breakdown in the logs if you want to dig further — sometimes people misread that as token-only.
[02:14] Sofia Martinez: Can you show the reranker flow? How does it expect the candidate set?
[02:20] Liam O'Connor: Sure. Two-step common pattern: 1) do a vector search to pull top-k documents (e.g., top 100), 2) call the reranker endpoint with those candidates + the query. The reranker returns a scored list and optionally a normalized score or label. Payload is JSON: query, candidates array with id and snippet.
[02:38] Tom Werner: Does the reranker accept dense vectors directly or only document text?
[02:43] Liam O'Connor: It accepts either. You can pass candidate vectors and we do dot-product fast-path, or you can send text snippets if you want the reranker to re-embed with a heavier context-aware model. There are tradeoffs — sending vectors is cheaper and faster, sending raw text lets the reranker use longer context for quality.
[03:02] Emily Zhou: Example latency numbers?
[03:06] Liam O'Connor: For hosted endpoints on our default instance: embeddings ~20-40ms per request for single batch (small batches), vector search/top-k query ~30-60ms depending on index size, reranker (when scoring 100 candidates) typically 120-300ms depending on model — smaller reranker models are ~120-150ms, larger context-aware ones are higher. These are typical p50/p95 ballpark numbers on our test workloads.
[03:33] Rajat Kapoor: If we need p95 < 200ms for UI, seems tight if reranker is 300ms. How do customers handle that?
[03:40] Liam O'Connor: Two common approaches: run the lightweight reranker (optimized quantized model) in front for UI, or use a hybrid where you do vector search + cheap rerank in the UI and have an offline heavy rerank for personalization. We also offer prefix/KV caching that reduces repeated token work — helps with sessions/FAQ style queries.
[03:58] Sofia Martinez: You mentioned quantization. Do you manage that, or do we need to tune models ourselves?
[04:03] Liam O'Connor: We provide recommended quantization profiles per model and workload. For hosted customers, we can apply verified quantized builds that maintain quality while cutting cost. We also expose model variants in the Console so you can A/B test.
[04:16] Maya Chen: Quick commercial note — OpalView: given the doc volume you mentioned earlier, you might fit well in a hosted pilot first, then evaluate Dedicated if you need guaranteed throughput.
[04:27] Emily Zhou: Okay. Can we see a live example with our sample set?
[04:31] Liam O'Connor: Let's run a toy query. I'm going to paste three sample docs and a query. This will call embeddings, then the reranker. You'll see the candidate payload and the final scores.
[04:45] (typing)
[04:50] [05:00] Liam O'Connor: Okay sending the request... Hmm small hiccup with a header, ignore that, retrying.
[05:08] [05:12] Sofia Martinez: No worries, screenshare lag.
[05:14] Liam O'Connor: All right results returned. You can see Doc B got top score — the reranker pulled in snippet context and bumped it above the top-k vector candidate. The Console highlights which tokens influenced the score.
[05:30] Rajat Kapoor: Could that token highlight leak PII? We do have some sensitive user data.
[05:36] Liam O'Connor: Good question. In hosted mode we strip high-sensitivity logs by default and you can enable only aggregated traces. For regulated data we recommend Private deployment with customer-managed KMS. For pilot, though, we can keep strict logging off.
[05:50] Emily Zhou: Any hard limits on candidate size? If we send 500 candidates, will the reranker handle it?
[05:56] Liam O'Connor: We support up to 1k candidates in the reranker payload, but latency scales. For large candidate sets we recommend pre-filtering (vector similarity + heuristic), or running a lightweight neural filter first.
[06:10] Maya Chen: Quick interjection — finance will want to see a simple cost estimate for a 1M-query month with average candidate size of 50. We have a template we can fill in if you want.
[06:20] Sofia Martinez: Yes please.
[06:22] Maya Chen: We'll include that in the benchmark spreadsheet.
[06:25] (brief pause)
[06:30] Liam O'Connor: A few technical details: embeddings are returned as 1024-d vectors (model variant dependent), we recommend L2-normalizing on client if you prefer dot-product. We also have an embeddings bulk endpoint that accepts up to 5k items per request for reindexing jobs, and has an async job pattern for very large indexes.
[06:50] Rajat Kapoor: How does the index store work? Is it a managed vector DB or do you integrate with existing indexes?
[06:55] Liam O'Connor: Hosted mode uses our managed index under the hood, but we have connectors for external vector DBs, and you can bring-your-own index in Private. For most folks the managed index reduces operational overhead.
[07:08] Tom Werner: Are there guarantees about consistency during reindex? Sometimes we do partial reindexes and need atomic swap.
[07:14] Liam O'Connor: We support versioned indexes and atomic rollovers — you can pin a route to a version and then flip after bulk load. Rollouts and canaries are supported in the Console.
[07:24] Sofia Martinez: Good. Could you also show how the Console surfaces per-route cost?
[07:28] Liam O'Connor: (navigates) yes — per-route charts show tokens, embeddings calls, reranker calls, and attributed spend. You can filter by model, time, and API key. That helps teams attribute costs to product features.
[07:40] Emily Zhou: Nice. Any way to emulate our traffic pattern for estimates? We have spikey traffic around promotions.
[07:47] Liam O'Connor: We have a traffic simulator that can replay a CSV of requests against the fleet to estimate p95 under load and cost. For spike protection we recommend autoscale + burst and route fallback to smaller models.
[07:59] Sofia Martinez: Could you outline a pilot plan? What would success look like?
[08:03] Maya Chen: Example pilot: 2 weeks, run on a held-out 1k-query test set, measure MRR and NDCG before/after, monitor p95 latency in UI, and measure unit cost per query. If we hit target NDCG lift and stay within latency/cost bounds, transition to a 90-day pilot with production traffic.
[08:21] Rajat Kapoor: That seems reasonable. What's the ramp to production? We have CI/CD restrictions and need SSO for API keys.
[08:27] Liam O'Connor: We integrate with SSO/SAML for Console access, and for API we support scoped API keys and service principals; RBAC hooks are available for Private deployments too.
[08:39] Emily Zhou: Any red flags around security? We need SOC2 type II and audit logs for vendors.
[08:46] Maya Chen: Redwood is SOC 2 compliant and we provide audit logs as an add-on. For very strict compliance we typically recommend Private, but many enterprise customers run hosted with our compliance package. We'll send the SOC2 kit.
[08:57] (brief side conversation, mute/unmute)
[09:05] Liam O'Connor: A couple optimization tips: 1) cache embeddings for frequently asked queries, 2) quantize reranker and use a smaller model in the retrieval path, and 3) use the reranker only for top 50-100 candidates — that usually gives most of the lift without the full cost.
[09:21] Sofia Martinez: What's the easiest way to integrate with our existing search pipeline? We currently use Elastic for text search and a separate vector store.
[09:28] Liam O'Connor: We have lightweight SDKs and examples that show: a) call your current vector store to get top-k, b) enrich candidates with snippets via a doc-lookup, c) call Redwood reranker endpoint and swap results. We can share a repo sample.
[09:42] Rajat Kapoor: Could you share the SDK code? We prefer Node but have some python.
[09:47] Liam O'Connor: Yep — I'll include both Node and Python snippets in the follow-up.
[09:52] Maya Chen: At this point any other blockers?
[09:56] Emily Zhou: Performance is main one. Also clarity on pricing for heavy reindexing so finance doesn't get surprised.
[10:02] Maya Chen: We'll include both steady-state and reindexing cost in the sheet.
[10:06] (longer pause, discussion about internal stakeholders)
[10:30] Tom Werner: Joined late — quick question: can the reranker emit feature attributions per doc so we can debug why something scored high?
[10:37] Liam O'Connor: Yes, we have an explainability flag that returns token/feature attribution snippets for each candidate. For hosted we limit raw logs; it's opt-in, but available.
[10:46] Sofia Martinez: Great.
[10:48] Maya Chen: Recap of next steps: Maya sends pricing + benchmark, Liam sends code samples and reranker payload examples, Rajat shares dataset. We schedule SE deep-dive week of Aug 10.
[10:59] Rajat Kapoor: I'll get the sample data to you by Aug 4.
[11:03] Emily Zhou: I'll review pilot metrics and share internal stakeholders.
[11:08] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow-up via email with the links to the Console recording and the benchmark spreadsheet.
[11:15] Sofia Martinez: Thanks all.
[11:20] (meeting ends)
